fib: ______ is the branch of biology that deals with the study of heredity (similarity) and genetic variations (differences).
Genetics
Genetics is the branch of biology that deals with the study of heredity (similarity) and genetic variations (differences).
______ is defined as the average age of the parents when their progeny are born.
Generation interval (GI)
Generation interval
GI
Generation interval (GI) is defined as the average age of the parents when their progeny are born.
______ is the tendency for successive records of the same animal to be more alike than those of different animals.
Repeatability
Repeatability is the tendency for successive records of the same animal to be more alike than those of different animals.
______ are those traits with continuous range of variation and do not fit into natural categories.
Quantitative traits
Quantitative traits are those traits with continuous range of variation and do not fit into natural categories.
______ are known collectively as gametes (gamos, Greek, meaning marriage).
Sex cells
Sex cells are known collectively as gametes (gamos, Greek, meaning marriage).
______ means that one record is a good guide to future ones and therefore, waiting is hardly needed.
high repeatability
A high repeatability means that one record is a good guide to future ones and therefore, waiting is hardly needed.
______ are those traits that are easily classified into distinct or discrete categories.
Qualitative traits
Qualitative traits are those traits that are easily classified into distinct or discrete categories.
______ refers to the observable or measurable difference among individuals within a population for a particular trait.
Phenotypic variation
Phenotypic variation refers to the observable or measurable difference among individuals within a population for a particular trait.
